about: Principles the Lead Game Designer and Game Design Critic use. 'apply' is a concrete instruction for the design definition; 'test' is how the critic verifies it.

patterns.principle: Every major action changes the future in a way the player can see.
patterns.apply: Each action declares preview drivers and at least one lasting state change (asset, relationship, reputation, capacity).
patterns.test: Action previews exist; bot sensitivity shows outcome change > 3%.

patterns.principle: Decide with estimates; truth arrives later.
patterns.apply: Hidden 'true' values with observed estimate bands; diligence/scouting actions narrow them; reveal at a scheduled moment.
patterns.test: At least one hidden-value field in the core loop.

patterns.principle: Good options cost something different: cash vs time vs reputation vs relationships vs risk.
patterns.apply: Event choices and action options must differ on at least two resource axes.
patterns.test: Choice effect vectors are not dominated.

patterns.principle: There is always more opportunity than capacity.
patterns.apply: Constrain by cash, capacity units (aircraft, theaters, roster spots), management attention (action points or slots), or time.
patterns.test: Bots leave > 30% of available opportunities untaken.

patterns.principle: Saying yes to one thing is saying no to another.
patterns.apply: Opportunities expire; capacity is exclusive; anti-portfolio tracks what you passed on.
patterns.test: Expiring opportunities exist.

patterns.principle: Bigger organization, bigger bets, bigger risks.
patterns.apply: Tiered progression unlocks larger actions with larger downside; stakeholder expectations scale with size.
patterns.test: Late-game actions have ≥ 5x early-game magnitude.

patterns.principle: The player can see how far they've come.
patterns.apply: Tiers/ranks with names, network/portfolio visuals that grow, history charts, milestones.
patterns.test: Tier definitions + growth visualization exist.

patterns.principle: Understanding the system makes you better.
patterns.apply: Explain drivers; skilled bots should beat random bots by a wide margin.
patterns.test: Skilled bot median score > 1.5x random bot.

patterns.principle: The world occasionally upends plans.
patterns.apply: World shocks (recession, price spikes, scandals) with warning signs and recovery options.
patterns.test: At least 3 world shock types; frequency 0.5–2 per game-year.

patterns.principle: Stories arise from interacting systems, not scripts.
patterns.apply: Events bind to real entities and conditions; rivals react to the player; people have careers that persist.
patterns.test: > 70% of events bind to entities.

patterns.principle: A named opponent makes success personal.
patterns.apply: Rival orgs with archetypes, memory of the player, head-to-head records, and news coverage.
patterns.test: Rival memory + head-to-head stats exist.

patterns.principle: People remember how you treated them.
patterns.apply: Relationship values on counterparties; negotiation and event outcomes depend on them.
patterns.test: Memory field used in at least one formula.

patterns.principle: The game remembers and retells.
patterns.apply: News archive, transactions, records, awards, milestone moments, annual review.
patterns.test: History module enabled with ≥ 3 record types.

patterns.principle: Setbacks are interesting, not terminal.
patterns.apply: Rescue options, distressed-asset bargains, restructuring, career continuation after firing.
patterns.test: Death-spiral detector passes.

patterns.principle: Big upside comes with real downside.
patterns.apply: High-variance options (bold expansion, star hire, aggressive leverage) with expected value close to safe options.
patterns.test: Variance spread between conservative and aggressive bots.

patterns.principle: Different players build different organizations.
patterns.apply: 2–4 viable archetypes (e.g., low-cost vs premium vs niche) supported by distinct actions/markets.
patterns.test: No single bot wins > 70% of runs.

patterns.principle: Celebrate firsts and records.
patterns.apply: Milestone moments with short dramatic copy, not walls of text.
patterns.test: ≥ 6 milestones spanning early/mid/late game.

patterns.principle: Something important is always coming.
patterns.apply: Home shows the next moment of truth (delivery, opening, earnings, season end) with a countdown.
patterns.test: Upcoming-moments list non-empty in > 80% of ticks.

patterns.principle: There are things to find.
patterns.apply: Talent/opportunity pools that refresh; hidden gems revealed by investment in scouting/research.
patterns.test: Opportunity pool refresh exists.

patterns.principle: Ownership feels tangible.
patterns.apply: Assets with identity (named aircraft, restaurants, theaters) shown visually.
patterns.test: Signature visualization of owned assets exists.

patterns.principle: Optimization is fun when it's strategic, chores when it's repetitive.
patterns.apply: Let the player set policies once; surface exceptions.
patterns.test: Click-burden detector passes.

patterns.principle: Long careers should leave a mark.
patterns.apply: Hall of fame, all-time records, decade reviews, retiring numbers, company history.
patterns.test: Legacy surfaces exist for long games.

patterns.principle: Crises are where players earn their stories.
patterns.apply: Critical events with moment presentation, multiple non-dominated responses, and follow-up consequences.
patterns.test: ≥ 3 critical event templates with follow-ups.

patterns.principle: Success must open new problems.
patterns.apply: Late tiers introduce new pressures (regulation, empire complexity, succession) and new ambitions (acquisitions, global expansion).
patterns.test: Late-game test: new actions/events appear after the top two tiers.
